fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: Healthy gums are the foundation of a healthy smile. Gum disease often develops quietly, without pain, so many people are unaware they have it until the condition has progressed. Left untreated, it can lead to receding gums, loose teeth and eventually tooth loss.

fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: At Precision Dental, we check your gum health at every examination and provide treatment designed to control inflammation and protect the structures that support your teeth.

sections.label: What Is Gum and Periodontal Disease?

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Is Gum and Periodontal Disease?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Gum disease is caused by bacteria in plaque that build up along and beneath the gum line. It generally occurs in two stages.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Gingivitis is the early stage. The gums become red, swollen and may bleed when you brush or floss. Gingivitis can often be reversed with professional cleaning and improved home care.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Periodontitis is the more advanced stage. Inflammation extends below the gum line, creating pockets between the gums and teeth, and the bone supporting the teeth begins to break down. Periodontitis cannot be reversed, but it can often be managed to help slow or stop further damage.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Is Gum Treatment Right for You?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: You may benefit from a gum assessment if you notice:

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Bleeding gums when brushing or flossing

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Red, swollen or tender gums

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Persistent bad breath or an unpleasant taste

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Gums that are pulling away from your teeth

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Loose teeth or changes in your bite

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Food catching between teeth more than usual

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Risk factors include smoking, diabetes, pregnancy, stress, certain medications and a family history of gum disease. Research also suggests links between periodontal disease and general health conditions such as diabetes and heart disease.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Happens at Your Appointment

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Periodontal Assessment

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We measure the depth of the spaces between your gums and teeth, check for bleeding and mobility, and take digital X-rays to assess the supporting bone. We then explain the stage of your gum health and recommend a plan.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Professional Deep Cleaning

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Periodontal treatment, sometimes called root planing or debridement, involves carefully removing plaque and tartar from beneath the gum line and smoothing the root surfaces so the gums can heal. Local anaesthetic is used to keep you comfortable, and treatment may be completed over one or more visits.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Review

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: After several weeks, we reassess your gums to measure how they have responded. If deep pockets remain, further treatment or referral to a periodontist may be discussed.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Maintenance

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Ongoing maintenance appointments with our dentist or oral health therapist are important for keeping gum disease under control.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Aftercare and Ongoing Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Your gums may feel tender and your teeth sensitive for a few days after deep cleaning. Rinse with warm salt water and continue gentle brushing. Long term, brush twice daily, clean between your teeth each day with floss or interdental brushes, and attend maintenance visits as recommended. Quitting smoking can significantly improve gum healing.

sections.label: Why Choose Precision Dental for Gum Treatment

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Why Choose Precision Dental for Gum Treatment

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We take gum health seriously and track changes carefully over time. Our team explains your results clearly, supports you with practical home care advice and offers happy gas for patients who feel anxious. Healthy gums are also essential before treatments such as dental implants.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The cost of your treatment depends on your individual needs. After your examination, we talk you through your options and the expected fees before any treatment begins. We accept most major health funds, process claims on the spot through HICAPS and are a preferred provider for {{site:preferredFunds}}. Interest-free payment plans are available through DentiCare for eligible patients, subject to terms and conditions. You can learn more on our Prices and Payment Options page.

fields.label: Small label
fields.value: FAQ

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Frequently Asked Questions

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can gum disease be cured?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Gingivitis can often be reversed. Periodontitis cannot be reversed, but with treatment and ongoing maintenance, it can often be managed and stabilised.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Is periodontal treatment painful?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Local anaesthetic is used during deep cleaning to keep you comfortable. Some tenderness or sensitivity afterwards is common and usually settles within a few days.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Why do my gums bleed?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Bleeding is often a sign of inflammation caused by plaque. It should not be ignored, even if it is not painful.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can gum disease cause tooth loss?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes. Advanced periodontitis can damage the bone supporting teeth, leading to loose teeth and, eventually, tooth loss.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: How often will I need maintenance appointments?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The frequency depends on the severity of your condition and how your gums respond. Many patients attend every three to six months.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Does smoking affect gum disease?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Smoking increases the risk of gum disease, can mask early warning signs such as bleeding, and slows healing after treatment.
